Hi Elena —

Short technical answers & next steps from the SE side:

1) Streaming + function annotations: yes. Redwood supports token streaming with interleaved function call annotations (we send function metadata as a side-channel in the stream so clients can pick up structured outputs as they’re produced).

2) Schema validation: we can surface schema validation failures as a 4xx structured error with a diff payload (we recommend validating client-side too for UX).

3) Latency profile: for 20–60 token UI charting we believe the quantized model + optimized kernel selection will meet the <150ms P95 on a c7-like instance with our runtime. For 60–120 token voice bursts we expect 200–260ms P95 in initial config; we’ll tune batching and KV cache for that flow.

4) Embeddings + rerank: plan is to run a two-stage pipeline — sparse/ANN retrieval -> embedding similarity -> small reranker (cheap transformer) for top-K reordering. We’ll provide sample tuning jobs for your dataset in the sandbox.

Actionables I’ll own:
- Run a profiler with your sanitized sample payloads once Priya sends them (ETA: 24–48h).
- Share a short reproducible benchmark (script + expected outputs) you can run in your environment.
- Prepare an SDK diff showing streaming API usage and the function-calling helper (attached in Marissa’s initial email).

If you’re open, propose the architecture sync for Wed 25 Feb 10–11am PT. I’ll build a 30-minute profiling slot into that meeting.

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.
